name: double_horiz_inputs
hypothesis: Doubling the input scaling for horizontal velocity and x offset makes the controller more sensitive to wind‑induced drift, encouraging earlier side‑engine thrust to counteract the strong horizontal wind and improve lateral control under higher gravity.

name: double_vert_vel
hypothesis: Doubling the input scaling for vertical velocity (and keeping the previous horizontal scaling) makes the controller more responsive to descent speed, causing earlier main‑engine braking under the stronger gravity. This should reduce crash speed and improve safe‑landing rates while retaining the improved lateral control from the earlier change.

name: scale_horiz_height_vert
hypothesis: Increasing the input scaling for horizontal offset (index 0) and horizontal velocity (index 2) by 2 preserves the improved lateral control from the previous best candidate. Adding moderate scaling (1.5×) for height (index 1) and vertical velocity (index 3) makes the network more sensitive to altitude and descent speed, encouraging earlier main‑engine braking under the stronger gravity. Slightly boosting body‑angle and angular‑velocity scaling (1.2×) helps maintain attitude stability in the presence of strong wind. Together these changes should reduce crash speed and increase safe‑landing rates while keeping the wind‑counteracting behavior.

name: input_horiz_vert_output_main_bias
hypothesis: Moderately increasing the scaling for height and vertical velocity (1.2×) while keeping the strong horizontal scaling (2×) improves sensitivity to altitude and descent speed, encouraging earlier main‑engine braking. Adding an output affine that boosts the main‑engine logit (scale 1.3, offset +0.2) and slightly suppresses side‑engine logits (scale 0.9, offset –0.1) biases the policy toward more timely vertical thrust without losing the lateral control gained from the horizontal scaling. This should reduce crash speed and raise safe‑landing rates under the strong gravity and wind.

name: horiz_vert_side_bias
hypothesis: Keeping the strong horizontal scaling (x offset and horizontal velocity ×2) to counter the 12‑unit wind, adding a modest increase to vertical‑velocity scaling (×1.2) to trigger earlier main‑engine braking under the stronger -11.5 m/s² gravity, and biasing the side‑engine logits upward (scale 1.2, offset +0.1) will improve lateral control without over‑braking. The main‑engine logit is left unchanged to avoid excessive vertical thrust. This combination should reduce crashes and increase safe‑landing rate.

name: horiz_vert_main_side_bias
hypothesis: Keep the strong horizontal scaling (x offset and horizontal velocity ×2) to counter the 12‑unit wind, add a modest vertical‑velocity scaling (×1.2) to trigger earlier main‑engine braking under the stronger -11.5 m/s² gravity, and bias both side‑engine and main‑engine logits upward (side engines scale 1.1, offset +0.1; main engine scale 1.3, offset +0.2). This should improve vertical braking while preserving lateral control, increasing safe‑landing and solution rates.

name: vert_scaling_main_bias_side_bias
hypothesis: Strong horizontal scaling (x offset and horizontal velocity ×2) counters the 12‑unit wind. Adding moderate height scaling (×1.5) and strong vertical‑velocity scaling (×2) makes the controller react earlier to descent speed under the -11.5 m/s² gravity. A modest increase to body‑angle and angular‑velocity scaling (×1.2) helps maintain attitude. Biasing the side‑engine logits upward (scale 1.2, offset +0.1) and the main‑engine logit strongly upward (scale 1.4, offset +0.4) encourages timely side‑thrust for drift correction and earlier main‑engine braking, reducing crash speed and improving safe‑landing rate.

name: mod_vert_main_side_bias
hypothesis: Keeping the strong horizontal scaling (x offset and horizontal velocity ×2) to counter the 12‑unit wind, adding a moderate vertical‑velocity scaling (×1.5) to trigger earlier main‑engine braking under the stronger -11.5 m/s² gravity, and slightly boosting the side‑engine and main‑engine logits (scale 1.05 for side engines with +0.05 offset, scale 1.2 for main engine with +0.1 offset) should improve both lateral drift correction and timely vertical braking, increasing safe‑landing and solution rates.

name: horiz_vert_main_side_small_bias
hypothesis: Strong horizontal scaling (x offset and horizontal velocity ×2) counters the 12‑unit wind. Adding a modest vertical‑velocity scaling (×1.1) makes the controller react earlier to descent speed under the -11.5 m/s² gravity. A small upward bias on both side‑engine logits (scale 1.05, offset +0.05) and a slight boost to the main‑engine logit (scale 1.1, offset +0.05) encourages timely side‑thrust for drift correction and earlier main‑engine braking without overwhelming the original lateral control. This should increase the chance of a safe, low‑velocity touchdown and raise the solution rate.

name: double_horiz_mod_vert_main_bias
hypothesis: Strong horizontal scaling (x offset and horizontal velocity ×2) already improves lateral control under the strong wind. Adding a modest increase to vertical‑velocity scaling (×1.3) should make the policy react earlier to descent speed without over‑reacting. A small upward bias on the main‑engine logit (scale 1.2, offset +0.1) encourages earlier braking under the stronger -11.5 m/s² gravity. Side‑engine logits are left unchanged to keep the good lateral behaviour. This combination is expected to raise safe‑landing and solution rates while improving mean return.

name: reduce_side_bias_vert_main_boost
hypothesis: Strong horizontal scaling (x offset and horizontal velocity ×2) continues to counter the 12‑unit wind. Adding moderate height scaling (×1.5) and a larger vertical‑velocity scaling (×1.5) makes the controller react earlier to altitude and descent speed under the -11.5 m/s² gravity. Reducing the side‑engine logits (scale 0.9, offset -0.05) discourages excessive lateral thrust, while boosting the main‑engine logits (scale 1.3, offset +0.2) encourages timely braking. This combination should lower crash rates and raise the chance of safe, low‑velocity touchdowns.

name: double_horiz_height_main_bias
hypothesis: Keeping the strong horizontal scaling (x offset and horizontal velocity ×2) to counter the 12‑unit wind, adding a moderate height scaling (×1.5) makes the controller react earlier to altitude, encouraging earlier main‑engine braking under the stronger -11.5 m/s² gravity. Adding a small positive offset to the main‑engine logit (+0.05) further biases the policy toward timely vertical thrust. This should preserve the good lateral control while improving vertical deceleration and increase safe‑landing and solution rates.
